These are area-wide estimates, not sale prices. Your own house may sit well above or below the median depending on age, lot, condition and school zone.

How does Gardner's weather affect a house?

Gardner has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. Rainfall averages 37.54 inches a year at the New Century AirCenter station, with May and June the wettest months.

Extremes run wide. The station's records include 114 degrees in July and minus 15 in February. Heavy spring rain, summer heat and hard freezes all test gutters, grading, sump pumps and roofing.

  • Check that downspouts discharge away from the foundation, since spring rain is the heaviest of the year.
  • Look at attic ventilation and insulation, because hot summers and cold snaps both load the cooling and heating system.
  • If a basement has water stains, buyers' inspectors will find them, so decide ahead of time how you will disclose and price them.

What permits and utility steps come with selling a Gardner house?

Gardner runs its own electric, water and wastewater utilities, so a sale involves city hall as well as the county. The city's utility billing page says an account holder must appear in person at City Hall, 120 East Main Street, to transfer service, with a connection fee of $10 per service or $15 for both. To stop service, contact the office before 3 p.m. on the day service should end.

Permits matter if you have done work on the house. Gardner requires building permits for projects such as finishing a basement, re-roofing, setting a shed, installing a sprinkler system or pool, and building a fence or deck. Contractors must hold a Johnson County Contractor's license, except fence and irrigation contractors, and homeowners who did the work themselves file a Statement of Homeowner Installation.

A buyer's inspector or lender may ask about permits for a finished basement or a new roof. Gather what you have before you list.

How are the deed and property tax handled in Johnson County?

Gardner deeds are recorded at the Johnson County Register of Deeds in Olathe. The county's fee schedule lists $21 for the first page of a deed or mortgage and $17 for each added page, and it charges nothing to file the sales validation questionnaire that Kansas requires with most deeds.

  • Johnson County takes eRecording and charges no extra fee for it.
  • The Kansas Department of Revenue calendar sets real estate tax payments at December 20 for the full or first half and May 10 for the second half.
  • Counties mail valuation notices by March 1, and the state calendar lists May 15 as the last day for an informal meeting with the county appraiser.

The title company ties these steps together at closing and prorates the tax between you and the buyer.

What do Gardner sellers usually face?

Gardner sellers are often deciding between a listing with showings and repairs, and a quicker sale as-is. The common reasons look like this:

  • Move on a short timeline. A job change within the metro or farther away can leave little time for staging and open houses.
  • Deferred maintenance. Houses built in the same years can reach roof and mechanical replacement age together.
  • Inherited houses. Heirs may live in other states and want one closing rather than months of upkeep.
  • Rentals. About one in three Gardner homes is renter-occupied, and owners who rent out a house sometimes decide to sell.

A cash offer fits those cases when you can accept the trade-off that a buyer pricing in repairs may offer less than a fully renovated listing would bring. Compare the offer against a listing's costs and wait time, then decide.

What should a Gardner seller ask any buyer?

Whether the buyer is an agent's client, a family or a company, the same questions protect you.

  • Is the offer for cash, and can the buyer show proof of funds?
  • Who orders and pays for the title search and closing, and which title company will handle it?
  • Is the house being bought as-is, and are inspections limited to a short window?
  • What closing date is offered, and can it move if you need more time to move out?
  • Will you be asked to sign anything before you see a written offer?

Written answers let you compare a cash offer, a listing and a sale by owner on the same terms. You owe nothing for asking.

More questions about Gardner, KS

How many people live in Gardner, KS?

The Census Bureau estimates 26,154 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 23,287 at the 2020 census and 19,123 in 2010.

Which county is Gardner in, and where do I record a deed?

Gardner is in Johnson County. Deeds are recorded with the Johnson County Register of Deeds, 111 S. Cherry St., Olathe. A real estate sales validation questionnaire must accompany most deeds under K.S.A. 79-1437c.

How do I transfer my Gardner utilities when I sell?

Gardner provides water, wastewater and electric service itself. Per the city's utility billing page, to transfer service the account holder visits City Hall in person and pays a $10 fee per service or $15 for both, and to terminate service you contact City Hall before 3 p.m. on the day.

Do I need a permit for work I did on my Gardner house?

Gardner requires permits for many projects, including re-roofing, basement finishing, decks, fences, sheds and pools. If you cannot find the permit for earlier work, tell the buyer and ask the city's Building and Inspections office what records exist.

When are Johnson County property taxes due if I sell in the spring?

Kansas sets the first half or full payment at December 20 and the second half at May 10. At a spring closing, the title company usually shows whether the second half is paid and prorates what remains.
